name: One Path, Two Stills
summary: The phone gets a pinned hero (an absolute 250lvh box at the top of .stage with a position:sticky 100lvh frame inside; nothing is reparented, nothing is fixed), a 4:5 phone encode of the cloche (frames 0-234, 640x800, ~0.9 MB) painted by the existing WebCodecs+WebGL path with one phone-only change (decoded frames become GL textures and are closed at once, so hardware decoder pools can never starve), a pre-blurred 6 KB still cross-faded over it by scroll (no runtime blur of any kind), a flat scrim for legibility, and ONE page-space SVG path for the line: born at the loop's open end the instant the frame un-sticks, curling under the plate to x=11, waving down the gutter with a fixed 4 px / 140vh wave, entering the mark's left lobe and drawing the figure-eight before the real mark fades in. The drawing law is the desktop's own: drawn length = arc length at the reading line (scrollY + 49vh), time-lerped, quantised, monotone, reversible. Everything hangs off html.story.snake, decided in the head script, so the desktop (html.film) and reduced-motion story never execute a new rule or statement. Two tiers only: WebCodecs film, or a blur-to-mark still cross-fade (Save-Data, no WebCodecs, decoder error, context loss). No <video> scrubbing, no CSS/SVG filters, no frame-space line, no measured keypoints, no DOM moves. Assets: hero-scrub-m.mp4, hero-m-blur.jpg (216x270), hero-m-mark.jpg (432x540, frame 234).

heroLayout: CLASS AND SCOPE. Every rule below lives under html.story.snake (site.css, new block before REDUCED MOTION; look-only rules in v-editorial.css after FINE TUNE). html.film never carries .snake; a reduced-motion phone never gets it; so both keep today's bytes. Default rules for the new elements are display:none. DOM (template, index.tpl.html; index.html regenerated). Inside .hero__frame after the canvas, two pictures with the site's own desktop-skip source so a desktop fetches 1 px gifs: and the same for class="hero__mark" with hero-m-mark.jpg 432x540 (loading="lazy" is fine here; it is needed only from u .55). Nothing else moves: #hero stays the first child of .stage where it is today, #snk and the tip are created by site.js and appended to .stage. The head gate adds/removes the class (see gating), so the pinned layout exists at first paint: no scroll-anchoring jump, no flash of the stacked story. THE PIN. html.story.snake{--pin:250vh;--pin:250lvh;--stage-pt:calc(var(--hdr-h) + clamp(28px,6vh,64px));--rail:11px}. .hero{display:block;position:absolute;left:0;right:0;top:0;height:var(--pin);z-index:0;overflow:visible;background:none;pointer-events:none} (absolute inside .stage, which is position:relative and starts at page y 0; top:0 is the padding edge). .hero.off{visibility:hidden}. .hero__frame{position:-webkit-sticky;position:sticky;top:0;left:auto;width:100%;height:100vh;height:100lvh;transform:none;background:none;overflow:hidden} (sticky inside an absolute containing block: it sticks while the 250lvh box is in view and un-sticks when the box's bottom reaches the frame's bottom, i.e. at scrollY = 150lvh; jitter-free, no JS). .band--hero{min-height:calc(var(--pin) - var(--stage-pt));padding-bottom:0} gives the in-flow page the same 250lvh, so the studio band begins exactly where the frame lets go. .band,.act{position:relative;z-index:2} so the bands paint over the film. .act--still{display:none}. Sticky needs no scroll container between the frame and the viewport: html/body use overflow-x:clip (site.css 70), main/.film/.stage stay overflow:visible; the gate requires CSS.supports('overflow-x','clip') so a browser that would fall back to overflow-x:hidden (which makes body a scroll container and kills sticky) never arms the snake. THE BOX (all layers share it). site.js layoutFilm() writes --bl/--bt/--bw/--bh on #heroFrame (px, once per build): bw = frame width; boxW = min(bw, LVH*1.1/1.25); boxH = boxW*1.25; bl = (bw - boxW)/2; bt = MARKY*LVH - MY*boxH with MARKY = .44 and MY = .535 (the mark's centre in the crop). 390x844: 390x487 at (0,110); mark centre (195,371); the lid, which reaches the crop's top at 4.2 s, never runs under the 52 px header. Layers, bottom to top, each position:absolute;left:var(--bl);top:var(--bt);width:var(--bw);height:var(--bh): .hero__mark img (z1, opacity var(--hm,0)); .hero__film canvas (z2, display:none until .hero.wc, opacity 0 -> 1 on .hero.video-ready with the existing .6s transition: story twins of site.css 336-338); .hero__blur img (z3, opacity var(--hb,1), will-change:opacity); .hero__frame::after (z5, background rgba(10,10,10,.84), opacity var(--hs,1), will-change:opacity). All four carry -webkit-mask-image/mask-image:linear-gradient(180deg,transparent 0,#000 12%,#000 88%,transparent 100%) so the box dissolves into the page's dotted ground (a #0A0A0A fade strip would blank the dots; the mask keeps them). .hero__video,.hero__pulses,.hero__ring{display:none} always. Frame background none, hero background none: the body's dot grid is the ground everywhere, the film floats in it. TEXT. The hero band's text is untouched (same type, same positions); under .snake only .btn--ghost wraps (white-space:normal, underline instead of the background hairline) so the arrow is not clipped at 390/360. .hdr.is-scrolled{backdrop-filter:none;-webkit-backdrop-filter:none;background:rgba(10,10,10,.86)} under .snake (no backdrop readback over the canvas). .ctabar switches on at y > heroTop + pinRange + .3*LVH (phone-gated line in onPageScroll) so it never parks on the pinned film. TOGGLES for Karan (read once when the snake arms, also settable from the preview switcher cookie): ?snake=off (today's story), ?snake=stills (force the still tier), ?hero=fit|cover (cover: transform:scale(var(--hz)) on the four box layers, origin 50% 53.5%, --hz from LVH/boxH to 1 over u .35-.75, compositor-only; default fit), ?rail=wave|straight.
filmPlacement:
ENCODE (cloche3d/encode-phone.sh, same x264 recipe as encode.sh): crop=864:1080:864:0 of the 1920x1080 PNGs (4:5, centre x 1296 = 67.5%: the closed cloche x 1020-1710 has 18 px of margin at the right, the held mark x 960-1620 / y 380-780 sits at x 11-88%, y 35-72% of the crop, centre (50%, 53.5%); the lifted lid's rightmost 72 px at 2.7 s are cut at the box edge while it leaves upward, acceptable), scaled to 640x800 lanczos, frames 0-234 (-frames:v 235, 7.833 s; frame 232 is the last fully closed loop, 233-234 the end just parted, 235+ the end lifts into the up-right unravel and is never encoded: constraint 4), keyint 8, keyint_min 8, sc_threshold 0, bf 0, High 3.1 (2000 MB/frame, 60k MB/s: inside level 3.1 for the widest hardware support), crf 24, bt709 tv, timescale 15360, faststart: about 0.85-0.9 MB. Stills: ffmpeg -i out/f0000.png -vf "crop=864:1080:864:0,scale=216:270:flags=lanczos,gblur=sigma=3" -q:v 6 hero-m-blur.jpg (~6 KB; the 1.8x CSS upscale plus dpr makes it softer still) and ffmpeg -i out/f0234.png -vf "crop=864:1080:864:0,scale=432:540:flags=lanczos" -q:v 4 hero-m-mark.jpg (~30 KB). Register all three in stamp.js (site.js tokens for the mp4 and the mark still's fallback URL; html assets for the two <picture>s), build_index.py, node stamp.js.

WHERE IT PAINTS. The canvas box is the 4:5 box above; the store stays the encode's native 640x800 (the phone branch of sizeFilmCanvas: if FD and heroFilm.width !== FD.mp4.width set width/height to the mp4 size; gl.viewport(0,0,640,800); ts = (1/640,1/800); bc = 0 so the Catmull-Rom path is off; drawnFrame = -1; paintSoon(); return). blit() draws its full quad into a store with the same aspect as the CSS box, so no object-fit and no stretch; the compositor upscales 1.8x at 390 px / dpr 3 (bilinear, invisible on a glowing subject) and 2.4x on a 768 px tablet at dpr 2 (soft but whole; an 864x1080 encode picked by (min-width:600px) is a later option, no driver change). Store size never follows the screen: an iOS toolbar collapse or a rotation costs one uniform update, never a canvas.width write (which would clear the backbuffer mid-scroll).

THE CLOCK. u = (scrollY - heroTop)/LVH, LVH = heroFrame.offsetHeight (100lvh, constant while the URL bar moves), heroTop and pinRange = hero.offsetHeight - LVH cached by phoneMeasure() (rebuilt on resize/fonts/ResizeObserver, never read on the scroll path). Film seconds t = track(PT_KEYS, u), PT_KEYS = [[.30,0],[.75,1.5],[1.30,5.8],[1.50,7.8]] (the site's own track(); the mark holds on frame 234 from u 1.5). Drive: the desktop's tick() easing, one rAF kicked by a passive scroll listener: pShown += (pTarget - pShown)*(1 - .84^(dt/16.667)), snap under .0003, loop idle when settled; pDraw() calls filmFrame(t) (which does wantFrame/filmDir, paintFrame, pumpDecoder exactly as on desktop) and writes --hb/--hs/--hm through setVar (quantised .01, so a settled frame writes nothing). hero.off + dropFrames() when scrollY > heroTop + 2.5*LVH + 40; visibilitychange visible, pageshow and webglcontextrestored call pDraw() so the picture returns without a scroll. The <video> element is never used on the phone.
blurMethod: A pre-blurred still, cross-faded by scroll; no runtime blur anywhere. hero-m-blur.jpg (frame 0 at the phone crop, 216x270, gblur sigma 3, ~6 KB) is an in the box above the canvas at opacity var(--hb): --hb = 1 - smooth(u,.35,.75) once the film is ready, 1 - smooth(u,.55,.95) while it is not (so the blur never clears onto a black box). Under it the film plays t 0 -> 1.5 s (steam) as the blur lifts, so the 'focus pull' and the first motion coincide. A flat scrim (.hero__frame::after, rgba(10,10,10,.84)) sits on top at opacity --hs = 1 - .85*smooth(u,.35,.75): with it the worst pixel behind the words (the blurred chrome rim and bokeh lights) is about #1F1A16, giving ink 14:1, sub (ink-2) 5.1:1, h1 line 2 (ink-3, 200 weight, 30.8 px) 4.6:1, acc 5.6:1; every word clears AA while any text is over the box (the buttons leave at 58vh, the scrim is still .66 there). The blur img and the scrim are will-change:opacity (two 390x487 layers, ~7 MB each at dpr 3) so their fades are compositor-only. Why not filter:blur() on the canvas: a Gaussian over a 1.7 Mpx layer on every canvas change is 2-6 ms on mid Mali/Adreno and re-rasterises on iOS, and blur(0px) still costs a filter pass unless class-toggled; why not a shader mip blur: more code in the shared painter for the same picture. Karan's habit: ?hero=cover shows the same cross-fade with the box scaled to cover the screen first, for a side-by-side on his phone.
lineBirth:
THE POINT. B = (BX, BY) = (.75, .62) of the box: the loop's bottom-right end, where frames 233-234 show the ribbon parting (engineer confirms from cloche3d/out/f0234.png cropped 864:1080:864:0; the two numbers are constants in site.js). Frame px: (bl + .75*boxW, bt + .62*boxH) = (292, 412) on 390x844. Page px (stage-relative) once the frame has un-stuck: (292, 1.5*LVH + 412) = (292, 1678).

THE WAKE (u 1.30 -> 1.50, frame stuck). The film plays 5.8 -> 7.8 s (the mark settles, the end parts). The one tip element (.snk__tip, a 72 px div in .stage: radial-gradient 2.2 px #FFF8EC core, halo to 36 px, will-change:transform,opacity; an inner span with a CSS keyframe breath scale 1 -> 1.25 over 1.6 s) is placed by JS in page space at (B.x, scrollY + B.y - stageTop) every rAF while u in [1.30, 1.50), opacity .7*smooth(u,1.30,1.45). A one-frame lag during a flick moves a soft halo by a few px: invisible. No frame-space SVG, no second tip, no handoff.

THE BIRTH (u >= 1.50). The first segment of the single page path is the curl from B to R0 = (xr, B.y + d) with xr = 11 (--rail: the middle of the 20 px gutter, a hair left), u_ = B.x - xr = 281, d = .27*LVH = 228: M B  C (B.x + .12u_, B.y + .30d) (B.x - .55u_, B.y + .62d) (xr + .22u_, B.y + .74d)  C (xr + .105u_, B.y + .80d) (xr, B.y + .88d) (xr, B.y + d). On 390x844: B(292,412) c1(326,480) c2(137,553) A(73,581) c3(40,594) c4(11,613) R0(11,640) in frame px, +1266 in page px. It leaves down-right continuing the lobe's exit (flip the .12 sign if f0234 shows the end pointing down-left), sweeps under the plate, crosses the gutter and dives into the rail with c4 directly above R0 so the tangent there is exactly vertical; every control point's y increases, so the curl is y-monotone and the same drawing law covers it. Lc ~ 420 px. The curl is drawn between scrollY 150vh and 177vh as the mark rises from 49% to 22% of the screen: the line pours out of the mark as it leaves. The gradient phase puts stop 0 (red) at B.y: the ribbon's free end is red-orange in the film; the tip shows the same.

WHY THE SEAM IS EXACT. The drawn end follows the reading line tipY = scrollY + K*LVH - stageTop with K = B.y/LVH (.488). At un-stick scrollY = heroTop + 1.5*LVH, so tipY = 1.5*LVH + B.y = B's page y: target length 0 at the very instant the frame starts to move, growing from the very point where the ribbon parted. Before un-stick tipY < B.y, target = 0, nothing drawn. No frame-space drawing, no coordinate handoff.
linePath:
ONE SVG, ONE PATH, PAGE SPACE. site.js creates <svg class="snk" id="snk"> once and appends it to .stage: position:absolute;left:0;top:0;z-index:3;overflow:visible;pointer-events:none; width/height ATTRIBUTES in px = stage.offsetWidth/offsetHeight, viewBox = 0 0 W H (never %, never a transform, never will-change: a 390 x 7400 px layer at dpr 3 would be a 26 Mpx promotion; unpromoted, Chrome re-rasters only the visible tiles the dash change touches, as the desktop's scenery already relies on). Coordinates are px relative to .stage's border box (stageTop measured once per build, ~0).

<defs>: #snkg and #snkglit, linearGradient gradientUnits=userSpaceOnUse spreadMethod=repeat x1=x2=0 y1={y1} y2={y1+Pp} with the desktop's eight #specg / #specglit stops (E5322B F2912F F3CB3C 5CB246 0FA3C2 2E5FA8 7A3E97 D51C73 at 0/13/26/40/55/70/85/100%; the lit set for the glow). Phase: red (stop 0) at B's page y, yellow (stop .26, what #infg shows at the mark's left extreme) at E.y: span = E.y - B.y; cycles = max(1, round(span/(1.6*LVH) - .26)); Pp = span/(cycles + .26); y1 = B.y. (~1300 px period, ~4 cycles down the page.) #snkPath (the line) and #snkLoop (the figure-eight). Threads: <g class="snk__g" style="--L:{Ls};--off:{Ls}"> with four <use href="#snkPath">: case (#000, 5 px, .55: lifts the line off the white clouds), glow (url(#snkglit), 10 px, .16: the bloom, no filter), body (url(#snkg), 2.2 px), core (#FFF6E8, .8 px, .5). .snk__g{fill:none;stroke-linecap:round;stroke-linejoin:round;stroke-dasharray:var(--L) var(--L);stroke-dashoffset:var(--off)} inherited by the uses, the desktop's law. A second group for the loop: lglow (url(#infg), width 2.6*--lw, opacity .14*(1 - --lb)), lbody (url(#snkg), --lw, opacity 1 - --la), lring (url(#infg), --lw, opacity --la*(1 - --lb)). url(#infg) resolves to the template's hidden defs across svgs, as the desktop's #loop uses it.

d = CURL + RAIL + ENTRY, built by buildSnake() from three measurements only (the frame box, .stage, the .storymark rect via offsetTop chain and offsetWidth/Height, so the story's translateY(18px) cannot fool it; under .snake .act--mark is transform:none anyway):
CURL: as in lineBirth, ending at R0 = (xr, B.y + .27*LVH).
RAIL (?rail=wave, default): a chain of half-wave cubics from R0 to S0 = (xr, E.y - .9h), amplitude A = 4 px (body 2.2 px stays inside the 20 px gutter; the glow may kiss the text edge at .16), half period hp = .7*LVH (one wave per 140vh, ~4-5 waves down the page). Extremes P_i = (xr + s_i*A, R0.y + i*hp), s alternating +1/-1 starting +1, for i = 1..n with n = floor((S0.y - R0.y)/hp) - 1; each segment C (P_i.x, P_i.y + .36hp) (P_{i+1}.x, P_i.y + .64hp) P_{i+1} (a sine-like half wave, tangent vertical at each extreme); the last segment goes from P_n to S0 with the same shape and x = xr, damping the wave onto the rail. ?rail=straight: L xr S0.y. No band or prop is measured: the line's rhythm is its own, so late fonts, lazy images and reveal transitions cannot move keypoints; only the mark's rect matters, and it is re-measured by ResizeObserver.
ENTRY: C (xr, E.y - .35h) (E.x, E.y - .45h) E, vertical out of S0, vertical into E (c2 directly above E).
LOOP (#snkLoop, px, no transform so dashes and --lw are px): the desktop's #loop re-based at its left extreme heading down, M8 60 C8 84 26 104 52 104 C78 104 100 88 100 60 C100 32 122 16 148 16 C174 16 192 36 192 60 C192 84 174 104 148 104 C122 104 100 88 100 60 C100 32 78 16 52 16 C26 16 8 36 8 60 Z, every point mapped by P(sx,sy) = (Rl + .090w + (sx-8)*.00445w, Rt + .161h + (sy-16)*.00770h) (mark-720.webp's centreline extremes at .090/.910 of w and .161/.839 of h; ribbon thickness .178w). E = P(8,60) = (Rl + .09w, Rt + .5h) = (106, Rt+60) at 390 (storymark 218x120, left edge 86).
The whole path is y-monotone by construction (every control point's y >= the previous one's), which is what the arc-length lookup needs. Ls ~ 5300 px (under the 65535 dash limit; if a tablet ever passes ~6000 px the path splits into two <path>s at a wave extreme, same law).

STACKING inside main (z-index 3 context): .hero z0 < .band/.act z2 < .snk z3 < .snk__tip z4 < .ctabar 80 < .hdr 90. Text starts at x 20, the line's glow ends at 16: they never meet; the full-bleed props (sky stills, the pair) are crossed on purpose.
lineDrawingLaw:
SAMPLE ONCE. After each build: Ls = snkPath.getTotalLength(), Ll = snkLoop.getTotalLength() (bail and retry next rAF if either is 0: the svg was display:none a frame ago); maps = sample(path, max(300, round(Ls/8))) (the desktop's sample(): xs, ys, ls arrays) for the line and 120 samples for the loop. atY(map, y): binary search on the monotone ys, linear interpolation of ls, clamped to [0, L]. atL(map, l): binary search on ls, returns (x, y). No getPointAtLength on the scroll path.

PER FRAME (one rAF kicked by a passive scroll listener, also by pageshow/visibilitychange/resize; nothing runs in the scroll callback but recording scrollY and scheduling):
  tipY = scrollY + K*LVH - stageTop                     (K = B.y/LVH, ~.488)
  target = tipY <= B.y ? 0 : atY(maps.line, min(tipY, E.y))   (0 before un-stick; Ls once the entry is reached)
  shownL = lerp(shownL, target, dt): shownL += (target - shownL)*(1 - .8^(dt/16.667)), snapped when |target - shownL| < .25 px; dt = min(100, now - last)
  setVar(lineG, '--off', Ls - shownL, .5)               (custom property on the group, quantised to .5 px: the style is touched only when the value moves; the uses inherit)
  lt = clamp((tipY - E.y)/(.7*h), 0, 1); shownLoop = lerp(shownLoop, lt, dt); setVar(loopG, '--off', Ll*(1 - shownLoop), .5)
  rb = smooth(tipY, E.y + .7h, E.y + .7h + .12*LVH); la = smooth(rb,0,.55); lb = smooth(rb,.45,1)

PROPERTIES OF THE LAW. Monotone and single-valued in scrollY: a flick draws forward through every point (the lerp never skips, the dash reveals every px), a scroll back rewinds smoothly, a reload mid-page lands on the right state on the first frame (hard = true sets shown = target with no lerp). The drawn end is always 49vh below the top of the screen: never under the header (6%), never under the contact bar (86%). Rebuilds (fonts.ready, .storymark load, ResizeObserver on .stage coalesced to one rAF, the 140 ms resize debounce, MQ changes) re-derive shownL = atY(newMap, tipY) and shownLoop from the same tipY, so a geometry change never animates. The film clock and the line clock are independent functions of scrollY: the film may lag a flick (decoder), the line never does.
CONSISTENCY WITH THE DESKTOP: same threads, same dasharray-on-the-group law, same sampled-map lookup, same time lerp, same #loop geometry, same 5 -> ribbon thickening and loop-out/mark-in crossfade; only the parameter is page y instead of world x.

performance: SCROLL PATH: the scroll listener (passive) stores scrollY and kicks one rAF; the rAF does: one filmFrame(t) (bind a cached 640x800 texture, one quad into the 640x800 store: 0.5 Mpx, no resample), 3 custom-property writes on #hero (--hb/--hs/--hm, quantised .01, skipped when unchanged; opacity on two will-change layers, compositor-only), one --off on the line group (quantised .5 px; Chrome re-rasters only the visible tiles the stroke crosses, ~1-3 ms on a phone; the SVG itself is unpromoted and has no transform), three loop vars and --rb/--rw only near the merge, one translate3d on the promoted 72 px tip. No layout read anywhere on the path: stageTop, heroTop, pinRange, LVH, the box, B, the storymark rect, the sampled maps are cached by buildSnake()/phoneMeasure(). Loop idle when settled (both lerps snap). Under 4x CDP CPU throttle the target is under 12 ms per frame; the first thing to trim if it is not is the glow thread's width (10 -> 6 px). DECODE: 8-frame GOPs, ~30 px of scroll per GOP at the lift; prefer-software when Android Chrome supports it (deterministic, no pool), hardware otherwise; phone pump lookahead [g, g+dir] and keepGops = 2, so at most 16 textures live (640x800 RGBA = 2.05 MB each, ~33 MB GPU) versus ~100 MB of 1080p VideoFrames today; the decoder's own frames are closed inside the sink right after texImage2D (1-2 ms each at this size), so MediaCodec/VideoToolbox output pools (8-16 buffers) never starve; textures are pooled (createTexture once, reused). The desktop keeps its VideoFrame cache and keepGops 4 untouched. MEMORY LIFECYCLE: hero.off (past the pin) and visibilitychange hidden call dropFrames() (phone: deleteTexture all, ~33 MB back); webglcontextlost -> dropFrames(); restore -> makePainter + the phone sizeFilmCanvas branch + pDraw(); pagehide -> close the decoder, keep the bytes; pageshow/visible -> re-init from bytes once, then stills. NETWORK: ~0.9 MB mp4 fetched after load at low priority, never on Save-Data/2g/prefers-reduced-data; stills 6 + 30 KB; the desktop's hero-still.jpg (48 KB) still downloads on the snake phone (display:none img) unless Karan accepts a coarse-pointer <source> skip. PAINT: two 390x487 promoted layers (blur, scrim) ~7 MB each at dpr 3, the canvas layer, the tip; the mask is per layer (four masks, each a compositor mask, no readback). NOT PROMOTED: the page-tall #snk, the bands. VIEWPORT UNITS: 100lvh for the pin and frame (constant through the iOS/Android toolbar collapse), never dvh; the reading line uses the measured frame height, not innerHeight, so the URL bar cannot move the drawn end; the resize handler ignores height-only changes under 25% when innerWidth is unchanged (no rebuild during the bar animation).
risks: iOS 16.4-16.x: VideoDecoder exists but texImage2D(VideoFrame) may throw; by design those phones drop to the still tier (blur-to-mark cross-fade, the line unaffected) rather than a 2D-context or createImageBitmap ladder. Verify on one real iPhone via window.__snake.state().tier; if that share matters to Karan, the 2D-context recovery is a contained addition later.

Hardware decoders on Android (MediaCodec) pay a codec flush per 8-frame GOP (30-120 ms); the phone slow check (250 ms per GOP average after six groups) and the 2.5 s flush watchdog hand off to stills. Prefer-software via isConfigSupported avoids it where Chrome ships the FFmpeg path; the texture sink keeps hardware safe where it does not. Needs one mid-range Android run (Chrome and Samsung Internet) reading state().cfg and groups.

position:sticky inside the absolute #hero relies on no scroll container between the frame and the viewport; html/body overflow-x:clip is fine, but any future overflow on main/.film/.stage silently kills the pin. Guarded by the CSS.supports('overflow-x','clip') gate (old browsers with hidden fall to the static story) and by the probe asserting heroFrame.getBoundingClientRect().top === 0 through the pin.

GPU memory: 16 textures at 640x800 (~33 MB) plus two 7 MB layers and the canvas; 2 GB Androids and old iPhones may still evict. Mitigated by dropFrames on hidden/off/context loss, keepGops 2, and the small encode; the store never resizes. If a device still loses the context repeatedly, the 576x720 encode (1.66 MB per texture) is a one-line asset swap.

A fixed-period rail ignores the beats, so a wave crest may fall beside a card's top edge or a still's seam by chance; it is a taste risk, not a correctness one (the line never enters the text column). If Karan wants crests on the headlines, the Catmull-Rom keypoint rail from the other design drops into the same law (still y-monotone) at the cost of measuring every band.

Samsung Internet: versions before 22 have no WebCodecs (stills tier by the gate), Save-Data is often on (stills), forced dark mode may re-tint the orange bar (add <meta name=color-scheme content=dark>). Firefox Android before 133 lands on stills. All are the designed degradation, not failures, but each should be seen once.

The mask on four layers (canvas, two imgs, the scrim) is standard, but a Safari build that mis-composites mask-image over a WebGL canvas would show hard box edges; fallback is a pair of gradient strips (loses the dots in a 12% band) or a dot-grid background on the frame with a JS-set phase.

Scroll restoration on reload mid-page and scroll-behavior:smooth jumps from the header: the film pumps through every GOP during a smooth jump and catches up via nearestFrame (as on desktop); the line is a pure function of scrollY so it lands correctly on the first frame. A jumping flag that pauses lookahead until scrollend is a small later refinement if the jump ever stutters.
